items.title: Section: Eating a Child's Flesh in the Desert — The Four Similes That Teach Disgust Towards Food

items.zh: 問：何等觸、意思、識食名麁？答：若在欲界。問：何等名細？答：若在色無色界。問：何等名為已生有情？答：若於現在已生增長。問：何等名為求有有情？答：若有希求未來諸有。問：何等名住？答：若無損害長養。問：何等名安？答：若攝受長養。問：已生有情，云何由食而得安住？答：如前所說道理應知。問：求有有情，云何由食攝受？答：由三門故，二種雜染增長。謂業、煩惱二種雜染，依識而有。由三門、雜染資長識故，諸求有者，於無間生攝受餘有。
items.en: Question: what makes contact, mental volition, and consciousness coarse? Answer: being in the desire realm. Question: what makes them subtle? Answer: being in the form or formless realm. Question: what is an already-born being? Answer: one currently existing and continuing to grow. Question: what is a being seeking existence? Answer: one longing for a future existence. Question: how is a being seeking existence sustained by food? Answer: through three doors, the two defilements of karma and affliction, both dependent on consciousness, increase; through this increase nourishing consciousness, such beings seize hold of their next existence without interruption.

items.title: Section: When Swallowed Food Actually Becomes Food, and Why Colour Doesn't Count

items.zh: 問：段食何時建立為食？答：於變壞時。若受用時，建立觸食。由彼攝受方得增益，是故段食三處所攝，謂香、味、觸建立為食，不立色處。
items.en: Question: when is solid food established as food? Answer: at the time of decomposition. While being consumed, it is instead established as the food of contact. Only once absorbed does it actually provide nourishment. Solid food is therefore subsumed under three sense-fields — scent, taste, and touch — never under the field of visual form.

items.zh: 由彼要至味勢熟等變壞之位，方損益故。

items.title: Section: Bitter Medicine, Sweet Poison, and the Invisible Wind That Feeds Beings in Hell

items.zh: 或有段物，於受用時有所損害，於變壞時方能攝益，如苦辛等。或有段物，於受用時暫為攝益，於變壞時乃為損害，如有甘美所不宜物。故變壞時方立為食，非受用時。問：更有所餘眾多行法住因可得，謂生、先業、神通、因緣合會、離障；何故但說此四為食？答：以多分故，易覺知故，於諸念住易趣入故，於日日分易資養故，唯此四種應顯為食。那落迦中無有段食，定地諸天亦復如是。諸那落迦，多由先業力所任持而得久住，雖有廣大諸根大種損害因緣，而不能死。然彼亦有諸微細風隨入身分，以之為食；難可了知，是故不說。
items.en: Some foods harm while being consumed yet nourish once decomposed, such as bitter medicines. Some foods nourish momentarily while being consumed yet harm once decomposed, such as sweet but unsuitable things. Hence food is established at the time of decomposition, not at the time of consumption. Because these four are the most common, most easily recognised, most readily entered through the foundations of mindfulness, and most in need of daily replenishment, only these four are revealed as food. Hell-beings have no solid food, nor do the gods dwelling in meditative absorption. Hell-beings, mostly sustained by the force of past karma, endure long despite vast harm to their faculties and elements, unable to die. Yet they too have an exceedingly subtle wind entering their bodily organs, serving as their food — too imperceptible to easily describe, and so not usually mentioned.

items.title: Section: One, Two, or Three — How Many Things Must a Faculty Depend On?

items.zh: 問：諸根依身轉，亦依境界耶？設依境界者，亦依身轉耶？答：若根依境界，必依身而轉。或有依身轉，而不依境界；謂諸有色彼同分根，以諸大種為依止故，說彼依身。問：若諸根有所依而轉者，彼一切皆一依耶？答：或有一依，謂諸有色彼同分根。或有二依，謂即有色同分諸根。或有三依，所謂意根及餘無色心法諸根，在有色界。若於無色，即此諸根唯有二依。
items.en: Question: do the faculties depend on the body, or also on their object? If they depend on their object, do they also depend on the body? Answer: if a faculty depends on its object, it necessarily also depends on the body. Some depend on the body without depending on the object — physical faculties not currently accompanied by consciousness, depending on the great elements. Question: if the faculties depend on something in order to operate, do they all depend on the same number of things? Answer: some depend on one thing — physical faculties without consciousness. Some depend on two — physical faculties with consciousness. Some depend on three — mind and the remaining mental faculties, within the form-possessing realms. In the formless realm, these same faculties depend on only two.

items.zh: 問：諸根是苦者，一切苦相合耶？設苦相合者，一切是苦耶？答：

items.title: Section: All Six Kinds of Skilful Understanding Now Fully Determined

items.zh: 或諸根是苦，而非苦相合，謂樂根、喜根。或有是苦，亦苦相合，謂苦根、憂根。或有是苦，非苦樂相，謂捨根。或有非苦，亦非苦相，謂後三根，苦對治故。問：諸根是善，彼根引樂耶？設根引樂，彼根是善耶？答：或根是善，而不引樂，謂憂、苦俱而修梵行，彼諸善根於現法中不能引樂。或根引樂，而非是善，謂諸無記及不善根，於現法中能引無記及染污樂。或根是善，亦能引樂，謂喜、樂俱修諸梵行所有善根，於現法中能引其樂。或根非善，亦不引樂，謂諸無記及不善根，於現法中能引諸苦。中嗢柁南曰：義、依處、證得、攝、食、由諸句。
items.en: Some faculties are painful yet not associated with the painful characteristic — pleasure and joy. Some are painful and also associated with it — pain and sorrow. Some are painful yet bear neither characteristic — equanimity. Some are neither painful nor associated with it — the final three, being pain's own antidote. Some wholesome faculties do not lead to pleasure — celibate discipline practised amid sorrow and pain. Some lead to pleasure without being wholesome — neutral and unwholesome faculties producing neutral or defiled pleasure. Some are wholesome and lead to pleasure — celibate discipline accompanied by joy and pleasure. Some are neither wholesome nor lead to pleasure — neutral and unwholesome faculties producing suffering. The middle summary verse states: meaning, basis, and attainment; subsumption, nourishment, and various propositions.

items.title: Section: Six Names, Six Meanings — A Compact Summary of Everything Just Determined

items.zh: 復次，具足攝持一切行義；具足攝持一切行義，是故名蘊。又有別義。常能增長諸業煩惱；常能增長諸業煩惱，是故名蘊。又有別義。常有所為及速滅壞；當有所為及速滅壞，是故名蘊。發起諸法；發起諸法，是故名界，是牽引義。能生能廣諸心心法；能生能廣諸心心法，是故名處。由眾緣故速壞集起；由眾緣故速壞集起，故名緣起。等起理趣；等起理趣，是故名處。若非理趣，說名非處。
items.en: Next, fully encompassing the meaning of all conditioned formations — fully encompassing the meaning of all conditioned formations is why they are named aggregates. There is a further meaning: constantly increasing karma and affliction — constantly increasing karma and affliction is why they are named aggregates. There is yet a further meaning: constantly active yet swiftly perishing — constantly active yet swiftly perishing is why they are named aggregates. Giving rise to phenomena — giving rise to phenomena is why they are named elements, this being the meaning of drawing forth. Generating and expanding mind and mental factors — generating and expanding mind and mental factors is why they are named sense-fields. Through conditions swiftly perishing yet accumulating and arising — this is why it is named dependent origination. Arising in accord with proper principle — this is why it is named valid; if contrary to that principle, it is named invalid.

blocks.text: The famous similes for food, and the end of the six skills that began in fascicle 53.
To teach disgust towards food, the sūtras compare it to eating one's own child's flesh in the desert to survive. Food is to be taken only to sustain the body for practice.
Master Cháng Bǎi: once chewed, altered, and digested, food is absorbed as nourishment; while swallowing, the mind delights: that is contact-food.
Bitter medicine nourishes; sweet poison harms. What counts as food is what sustains.
Master Cháng Bǎi: mind depends on body, object, and mind to arise; in the formless realm only on mind and object.
Master Cháng Bǎi: the first meaning shows the aggregates are conditioned; the second, that they are contaminated. An element is a seed, from which things manifest.
The child's-flesh simile is shocking on purpose. It is meant to cut the craving for taste, not to make eating a burden.

quiz.q: The English has "at the time of decomposition." Does this fit the lecture, and what counts at the time of consumption?
options: the lecture means after chewing and digestion; "decomposition" suggests rotting, "digestion" fitting better; swallowing is contact food
it fits exactly: food must first rot, and swallowing is also solid food
no: it should be cooking; consumption is consciousness food
no: it should be purchase; consumption is volition food
quiz.why: Master Cháng Bǎi: after the food is chewed, altered, and digested, it can be absorbed as nourishment; while swallowing, the mind delights and the faculties are pleased, and this is contact food, not solid food. 變壞 here is change through digestion. "Decomposition" in English suggests rotting.

quiz.q: What have one, two, or three supports, and what of the formless realm?
options: physical with consciousness one; without two; mind in the formless three, in form realms two
physical faculties without consciousness one; with consciousness two; mind and mental faculties in form realms three; in the formless two
quiz.why: Master Cháng Bǎi: mind and mental faculties depend on body, object, and mind in order to arise; in the formless realm they depend only on mind and object. Physical faculties without accompanying consciousness have only the body. The English "without consciousness" is a fair gloss of 彼同分.

quiz.q: How does Master Cháng Bǎi explain the three meanings of aggregate and the meaning of element?
options: the first shows unconditioned, the second uncontaminated; elements are the four great elements, unrelated to seeds
the first shows conditioned, the second contaminated; an element is a seed, from which phenomena appear, so named
one meaning only; elements are worlds
aggregates are bodies; elements are lands
quiz.why: Master Cháng Bǎi: the first meaning shows the aggregates to be conditioned, and the second, contaminated. An element is a seed, from which phenomena manifest, and so it is provisionally called an element. This matches the treatise's gloss of drawing forth, kept by the English.
